The eastward tunnel takes a bend to the north, where it becomes a set of slick stone stairs. The trickle of water stems from between the crumbled remains of what was once a burial alcove; there is a rusted metal door leading to the room on the eastern side of the passageway.
The air is thick with the smell of stale water and decay. Faint dripping echoes from the darkness.
Stone walls covered in moss narrow the passage. A cold draft sweeps from the north.
The floor is uneven, littered with broken pottery and bones. The ceiling is low here.
